stem: Under what circumstance is abdominal pain and vomiting considered a sign of anaphylaxis rather than a mild to moderate reaction?

options.text: When it occurs more than 2 hours after eating
In the case of an insect-related allergic reaction
When it is accompanied by localized hives
Whenever it occurs in a child under age 5

explanation: The source notes a caveat: in insect reactions, abdominal pain and vomiting are signs of anaphylaxis.
rationale: Consider the type of allergen source that changes the severity classification of gastrointestinal symptoms.

optionExplanations.A: The timing doesn't change the classification of the symptom from mild to severe in food reactions.
optionExplanations.B: The source notes a caveat: in insect reactions, abdominal pain and vomiting are signs of anaphylaxis.
optionExplanations.C: Hives combined with abdominal pain in food allergy still typically fall under the mild-moderate category.
optionExplanations.D: Age does not change the classification of this specific symptom for food allergies.
